title: Catalogue transcription and digital availability audit
kind: The library and its digital copies
question: Which books does the La Flèche catalogue record, which predate 1737, and which have a usable digital copy?
what_was_done: The manuscript catalogue of the college library was transcribed into a structured list. Each pre-1737 entry was checked for a digital copy and the match graded by confidence. A first acquisition shortlist and a processing queue were built from the result.
result_summary: The record gives 2,493 catalogue entries, 1,899 of them pre-1737, and 838 pre-1737 texts with a high- or medium-confidence digital match. A later count (19 April 2026) identifies 722 French-language texts by a title heuristic, with 38 profiled, 311 digitised but unprocessed and 394 with no known digital source; those three figures do not sum to 722 in the record.
statistics: Catalogue entries transcribed: 2,493 | Entries dated before 1737: 1,899 | Pre-1737 texts with a high- or medium-confidence digital match: 838 | French-language texts identified by title heuristic (19 April 2026): 722 | First acquisition shortlist: 10 first-tier and 6 second-tier texts

title: Readiness inventory of French works for page-anchored study
kind: The library and its digital copies
question: Which French works held by the project were ready for a discovery pilot whose passages could be cited by page?
what_was_done: Sixty-four French candidate folders were inspected read-only against the project's identity, dating, page-provenance and corpus records. Each was classed by what stood between it and a citable, page-anchored run. Four works were then frozen for the first pilot without any retrieval output being used to choose them.
result_summary: Four works were frozen for the pilot and two more were ready; 15 needed a page-provenance build, 7 needed witness or locator work, 8 were post-1737 and usable only as controls, 26 lacked a governed identity (21 works and 5 tomes) and 2 were blocked by a contamination record. The report's conclusion is that 'the bottleneck is passage provenance, not text'.
lessons: The bottleneck is passage provenance, not text.
statistics: French candidate folders inspected: 64 | Works frozen for the first pilot: 4 | Ready with page anchors, deferred: 2 | Needing a page-provenance build: 15 | Needing witness or locator work: 7 | Blocked for lack of a governed identity: 26 (21 works, 5 tomes) | French works with citation-grade page anchors before the task: 5

title: Acquisition and OCR of four further French texts
question: Could four further French works be acquired from early editions and machine-read cleanly?
what_was_done: Four texts passed a source gate and were submitted together for download and OCR: Malebranche's Traité de la nature et de la grâce (1684), Fénelon's Démonstration de l'existence de Dieu (1718 collected edition), Malebranche's Traité de morale (1684 first edition, to replace a contaminated 1882 reprint) and Silhon's De l'immortalité de l'âme (1634).
result_summary: As of 17 May 2026 two texts had completed OCR and were synced (364 of 364 and 601 of 601 page files). The Traité de morale download had failed transiently and awaited retry, and the Silhon identifier resolved to a 69-view fragment, so that text was recorded as blocked for an incomplete source. Later states of the two unfinished texts were not read for this draft.
statistics: Texts submitted: 4 | Texts with OCR complete and synced: 2 | Texts with a failed download: 1 | Texts blocked for an incomplete source: 1

title: Structural preprocessing and dialogue re-ingestion of four works
question: Can source order, material type, page anchors and speaker labels be fixed deterministically for four works before any retrieval?
what_was_done: A structural preprocessing regime was applied to four works: source order was verified from scan pages, every paragraph was given a material status (authorial, apparatus, front or back matter, uncertain) and page anchors were attached. Malebranche's Entretiens was re-ingested so that merged dialogue turns were split and speakers labelled. Hume-side paragraphs were flagged descriptively.
result_summary: 4,551 of 4,662 paragraphs received scan-page anchors and every paragraph a recorded material status. The pilot report says the regime prevented the earlier failures only 'partly': it prevented source-order errors, unknown witnesses and missing speaker labels, but not the Hume-side Latin-quotation magnet, because its flags are descriptive and have no effect on rank. The dialogue split helped reading and attribution; whether it changed rank quality was not measured.
lessons: Descriptive flags do not change ranking: the Hume-side Latin-quotation magnet was not prevented, because the flags have no effect on rank. | Speaker labels make voice explicit: a speaker's doubt in a dialogue is not the author's endorsement.
statistics: Paragraphs with scan-page anchors: 4,551 of 4,662 | Hume paragraphs flagged descriptively: 152 of 1,468 | Entretiens paragraphs with a speaker label in the witness: 425 (218 not asserted) | Entretiens queue rows that are split pieces of formerly merged paragraphs: 27 of 50

title: Re-OCR and short-fragment filter for badly scanned prints
question: Can a second OCR pass and a minimum paragraph length make badly scanned early French prints usable for extraction?
what_was_done: Scans were re-read with an OCR engine and model trained on early print, paragraphs were rebuilt from page layout, and fragments under 80 characters were dropped at ingestion. The workflow was developed on one text and confirmed on three others. A rule-based classifier of structural units and page-region masking were tried as alternatives to the simple filter.
result_summary: The record treats the workflow as confirmed on four texts: extraction failure fell from 46% to 0.0% on the development text and, on Boullier's Essai, from 62.0% to 13.9% for one Hume pairing and from 42.0% to 8.6% for another once short fragments were filtered. The record adds that the gains mix better OCR with changed paragraph granularity and the two effects are not separated. The rule-based classifier did not beat the filter; page-region masking helped one margin-heavy text and not another.
lessons: Structural-fragment pollution, not character-level OCR quality, was the primary observed failure mode. | An extraction-failure gate (under 20%, 20 to 35%, over 35%) makes OCR quality a first-class operational concern.
statistics: Extraction failure, development text: 46% to 9.4% to 0.0% with the filter | Extraction failure, Boullier against EHU 9: 62.0% to 19.4% to 13.9% with the filter | Extraction failure, Boullier against THN 2.3: 42.0% to 8.6% with the filter | Extraction failure, La Placette and Cureau: 3.2% and 2.6% | Raw paragraph-reconstruction accuracy on a ten-page sample: 75%

title: Line-merging repair for narrow-column texts
question: Does merging short lines during reconstruction repair narrow-column texts without damaging clean ones?
what_was_done: An optional line-merging step was added to paragraph reconstruction and tried on two narrow-column texts. It was then run across a seven-text regression set to check for loss of content.
result_summary: Short-fragment rates fell from 66.8% to 29.3% on Babin and from 59.6% to 19.8% on Buffier, with standard-layout texts essentially unchanged and zero content loss across the seven-text regression set. The step stayed off by default and is invoked per text. Babin remained blocked for other reasons (a reconstruction failure and a bilingual body).
lessons: Reconstruction and preflight are judgment-gated: two texts with similar fragment metrics needed different diagnoses and different responses.
statistics: Short-fragment rate, Babin: 66.8% to 29.3% | Short-fragment rate, Buffier: 59.6% to 19.8% | Content loss across the regression set: 0 in 7 texts

title: Detection and removal of editorial matter in scanned sources
question: Were early results inflated by scanning boilerplate, editors' introductions or variorum notes in the source files?
what_was_done: An audit of Malebranche's Traité de morale against Hume's religion texts was declared invalid when the source proved to be an 1882 critical reprint carrying editorial matter. Contaminated paragraphs were removed from that text and from one other, the affected runs were repeated, and the remaining candidates were checked. Hume-side paragraphs with missing section labels were re-sectioned or tagged as apparatus.
result_summary: In the 1882 reprint, 260 of 1,244 paragraphs were editorial or scanning matter; after removal the text's concentration on the religion texts fell from 46% to 34%. Fourteen boilerplate paragraphs were removed from Nieuwentijt, 19 unlabelled Hume paragraphs were fixed, and the other candidates (about 39) were recorded as clean. The 1882 reprint was later marked never to be reused and a 1684 first edition was sought in its place.
hume_scope: Dialogues concerning Natural Religion; Natural History of Religion
lessons: Scanning front matter, editorial introductions and variorum notes inflated early rankings.
statistics: Paragraphs removed from the 1882 reprint of the Traité de morale: 260 of 1,244 | Concentration on the religion texts before and after removal: 46% to 34% | Boilerplate paragraphs removed from Nieuwentijt: 14 | Unlabelled Hume religion paragraphs fixed: 19

title: Early single-text discovery runs before the first campaign
question: Does a fixed retrieval-and-scoring pipeline separate texts with concentrated structural contact from background and noise?
what_was_done: About ten French texts were run one at a time against the unified Hume corpus: fifty top-ranked pairs per text were scored by a small scoring model and a book-level verdict recorded. A book-advancement threshold was fixed from these runs.
result_summary: Recorded verdicts ranged from 'advance' (Malebranche's Recherche, a calibration pass that nevertheless missed the well-known occasionalism locus) through 'moderate' or 'broad' signal (Montaigne, Cureau, La Placette) to 'likely noise' (Nicole, Simon) and 'does not advance' (Nieuwentijt). These are early machine verdicts: the Recherche result was later overturned by audit, and the Traité de morale run was withdrawn because its source was a contaminated reprint.
hume_scope: Unified Hume corpus (Treatise and first Enquiry)
lessons: Raw pass rate alone is unreliable; the number and quality of top-scored pairs discriminate better. | A documented relation can fail to surface because of a vocabulary-register mismatch at retrieval.
statistics: Malebranche's Recherche, pairs at the top score: 5 | Montaigne, passing pairs: 12, none at the top score | Cureau de La Chambre, passing pairs: 20, none at the top score | La Placette, passing pairs: 11, one at the top score | Nieuwentijt, passing pairs: 19 (51.4%), none at the top score | Ramsay's Histoire de Turenne, passing pairs: 3 (6%), none at the top score

title: First screening campaign over the French philosophy shelf
question: Which texts in the French philosophy section of the catalogue show concentrated structural contact with Hume under one fixed pipeline?
what_was_done: Sixteen eligible texts were taken through source inspection, OCR, a fixed retrieval-and-scoring pipeline and a per-text dossier. Fifty top-ranked pairs per text were scored by a small scoring model, and a book-advancement threshold fixed beforehand was applied.
result_summary: Ten texts were scored and four were blocked before scoring (a wrong edition, an incomplete volume, a reconstruction failure, and a text found to be a paraphrase of Aristotle). Only Arnauld's Des vrayes et des fausses idées advanced, on a twelve-pair concentration at THN 1.4.2; nine did not advance. The project's recorded conclusion is that the campaign 'surfaces structured contact zones at varying levels of abstraction, not influence'.
hume_scope: Unified Hume corpus (Treatise and first Enquiry)
lessons: Commentary or paraphrase texts without an independently recoverable authorial voice are structurally unsuitable for the instrument. | A non-zero count of top-scored pairs does not advance a book when the pairs are scattered and form no concentrated zone. | Blocks differ in cost by when they occur: at source inspection, after OCR, or after reconstruction.
statistics: Eligible texts: 16 | Texts scored: 10 | Texts advancing: 1 | Texts blocked before scoring: 4 | Passing pairs of 50, Arnauld: 23 (3 at the top score) | Passing pairs of 50, range over the nine non-advancing texts: 8 to 22

title: Batch profiling of the moral-controversy shelf
question: What do retrieval profiles look like when a whole catalogue section is processed together?
what_was_done: Nineteen texts from the catalogue's section of moral controversies were chosen for tractability and not for predicted relevance. The first seven were processed end to end and profiled against Hume's sections, and a triage memo ranked them for inspection.
result_summary: Two recurring profile regions were observed: Treatise 3.2 to 3.3, expected for moral theology, and the first Enquiry 10 to 12, which was unexpected and appeared in texts on ecclesiastical authority and against Jansenism. These are retrieval-level profiles, not audited findings. Twelve texts were still in OCR when the record was written; their outcome was not read for this draft.
statistics: Texts in the batch: 19 | Texts processed end to end at the time of the record: 7

title: Validation of the section-profile map as a triage surface
question: Can a text's distribution of matches across Hume's sections be trusted as a first triage signal?
what_was_done: Six texts with different profile shapes were inspected by hand to see whether the shape of each profile corresponded to something real in the text. The cases were classed as concentrated, broad, split or artefactual.
result_summary: The recorded conclusion is that 'retrieval-level triage is effective; interpretation must operate at cluster/profile level'. Of the six cases, one concentration was confirmed (Arnauld), one was a retrieval artefact (Nieuwentijt), one was broad alignment (Condillac), one was a split profile (Crousaz's Examen), one was judged concentrated and real (La Placette) and one was left pending (Boullier). Text-by-text validation was then discontinued.
lessons: A concentrated profile can be real or artefactual; shared vocabulary without engagement on the problem produces concentration too.
statistics: Texts inspected: 6

title: Parallel comparison against Hume's writings on religion
question: Do theological texts profile more sharply against Hume's religion texts than against the Treatise and first Enquiry?
what_was_done: Hume's Dialogues and Natural History of Religion were prepared as a separate comparison corpus. Three texts from the moral-controversy batch were profiled against both corpora, and the layer was later extended to 41 texts. It was kept as a parallel layer and not merged into the baseline.
result_summary: In the three-text trial, concentration rose from about 20-28% against the baseline corpus to about 32-40% against the religion texts, and the spread narrowed from about 30 sections to 18-20. The record treats differences between the two layers as diagnostic and requires a versioned decision before any merge.
hume_scope: Dialogues concerning Natural Religion; Natural History of Religion
statistics: Paragraphs in the religion comparison corpus: 406 in 29 sections | Texts in the trial: 3 | Texts profiled against the religion texts by the later record: 41 | Concentration, baseline against religion corpus: about 20-28% against about 32-40%

title: Yield check on two re-ingested texts
question: Does a re-ingested, body-only version of a text yield top-scored pairs when sampled beyond the usual fifty?
what_was_done: Two further French texts were re-ingested with a newer ingester and run through the fixed retrieval. For one, 80 sampled pairs were scored and seven floor-level cases were read by an external blinded model reviewer. For the other (Crousaz's Logique) the old and new queues were compared.
result_summary: The first text yielded no pair in the top score range among the 80 sampled; one possible case of floor leakage was quarantined without adjudication, and the line was closed for the time being. For Crousaz's Logique the queues differed between versions but the older run's provenance was 'not clean enough for a yield conclusion', so no scoring was spent. The record leaves the overall yield verdict pending and allows no claim that either text shows no signal.
statistics: Sampled pairs scored on the first text: 80 | Pairs in the top score range: 0 | Floor-level cases reviewed: 7 (1 quarantined)

title: Audit of Arnauld's Des vrayes et des fausses idées
question: Is the concentration of Arnauld's matches at Treatise 1.4.2 substantive at pair level?
what_was_done: The top-ranked Arnauld pairs against the baseline Hume corpus were audited pair by pair, with structural diagnostics for apparatus, duplicated Hume paragraphs and dispersion. A scholarly report then set out hypotheses for testing.
result_summary: The audit was recorded as positive: a contact zone at THN 1.4.2 with a core of four substantive, text-specific pairs on representative intermediaries, presence to the mind and the existence of bodies. It also recorded a layer problem, since Arnauld quotes Malebranche at length. Arnauld was the only text to advance from the first campaign; the findings document describes this text as later than 1737, whereas the holder's record of the scanned copy gives 1724 (see the work's page); it also notes that the result was never re-adjudicated under the later review contract.
lessons: The audit recorded a layer problem: Arnauld quotes Malebranche at length, so a match can come from either voice.
statistics: Pairs concentrated at THN 1.4.2 in the campaign run: 12 | Substantive, text-specific core pairs in the audit: 4

title: Two null audits against Hume's religion texts
question: Do the apparent matches of Bonichon and Nieuwentijt with Hume's religion texts hold up at pair level?
what_was_done: Top-ranked pairs for Bonichon's Authorité episcopale and for Nieuwentijt's Existence de Dieu against Hume's religion texts were audited pair by pair, with dispersion and apparatus diagnostics.
result_summary: Both audits were recorded as null. Bonichon was a thematic mismatch. Nieuwentijt showed topic-vocabulary retrieval with maximum dispersion and matches running in the opposite direction (assertions paired with critiques of them).
hume_scope: Dialogues concerning Natural Religion; Natural History of Religion
lessons: Maximum dispersion on the candidate side (fifty different paragraphs in fifty pairs) is a reliable sign of topic-level retrieval without argumentative convergence.

title: Audit of Descartes's Méditations against the Dialogues
question: Is the match between the Méditations volume and Hume's Dialogues substantive, and in which layer of the volume does it lie?
what_was_done: Top-ranked pairs between the French Méditations (with Objections and Replies) and Hume's religion texts were audited pair by pair. The layer of the volume each pair came from was recorded.
result_summary: Recorded as positive: a contact zone at Dialogues part 9 (self-causation, necessary being) with 2 substantive and 5 analogical pairs. The signal was concentrated in the Objections and Replies and not in the Meditations proper, so it does not generalise to the primary text. The scholarly report graded the case 'Plausible'; the records read for this register show no later re-adjudication.
lessons: In a composite volume, note which authorial layer carries the signal.
statistics: Substantive pairs: 2 | Analogical pairs: 5

title: Pair-level audit of the first campaign's ten scored texts
question: What kinds of signal lie behind the scores the first campaign produced?
what_was_done: All ten scored texts were audited pair by pair in a workflow using two model auditors from different families. The audit classifications were then compared across three works by Malebranche in different registers and across two editions of Régis.
result_summary: The audit grounded a seven-category taxonomy of signal types (from doctrinal engagement to domain-misaligned structural signal), each with at least one example, recorded as 'provisionally validated'. Its main recorded finding is a shift in what is measured: the campaign 'surfaces structured contact zones at varying levels of abstraction', not influence. 'Systematic inflation' was named as a risk for system-building authors.
hume_scope: Unified Hume corpus (Treatise and first Enquiry)
lessons: Audit-layer integration is a necessary component of the instrument, not an optional refinement. | Dense systematic structure produces coherent high-scoring signal on tradition-level material; the audit layer has to downgrade it. | Audit classifications stayed the same across two editions of one work although the surface metrics differed.
statistics: Texts audited: 10 of 10 scored | Signal-type categories: 7

title: Audit of Huet's Traité against both Hume corpora
question: Where, if anywhere, does the French text of Huet's Traité show substantive contact with Hume?
what_was_done: Top-ranked pairs for the French Traité philosophique de la foiblesse de l'esprit humain were audited against the baseline Hume corpus and, separately, against the religion texts. It was the first case analysed against both corpora.
result_summary: Against the baseline the audit was positive but narrow: one substantive and one text-specific pair at the first Enquiry section 12, while an apparent concentration at THN 1.3.15 was an artefact of short numbered rules. Against the religion texts it was 'partial': no substantive pair and four text-specific ones at Dialogues parts 1 and 9. The report's grade ('Plausible', localised to EHU 12) was not re-adjudicated later.
lessons: Short numbered rules attract matches by format, not content.
statistics: Substantive pairs against the baseline corpus: 1 | Substantive pairs against the religion texts: 0 | Text-specific pairs against the religion texts: 4

title: Baseline audit of Malebranche's Recherche de la vérité
question: Does the fixed pipeline retrieve Malebranche's own argument in the Recherche?
what_was_done: The fifty top-ranked pairs for the Recherche against the baseline Hume corpus were audited pair by pair. The missing occasionalism locus was then traced through the pipeline to see where it was lost.
result_summary: Recorded as 'uniformly negative': no substantive pair, 34% of the candidate side was apparatus, and the pipeline found an editor's gloss in place of Malebranche's prose. The scholarly report graded the case 'Inconclusive (pipeline-limited null)' and the record attributes the null to a limit of the instrument, a gap of vocabulary and register, and not to the texts.
lessons: A null result can mark a boundary of the instrument: a documented relation may be undetectable because of register mismatch. | Historical context does not override an audit classification.
statistics: Substantive pairs in the audited top fifty: 0 | Candidate-side apparatus noise: 34%

title: Panel review of a Bergier cluster on miracles
question: Does a localised cluster of Bergier pairs at Hume's section on miracles survive review by a model panel?
what_was_done: Eight pairs between Bergier's La Certitude des preuves du christianisme and the first Enquiry section 10 were reviewed by a model panel. A scholarly lead report was written, with a principal investigator disposition on how to proceed.
result_summary: Six of the eight clustered pairs were retained by the panel as strong advisory cases, and re-aggregating the same panel results under the later, stricter rule still retained about 75%, against 11% for a dispersed Bergier sample. The pair set became a calibration anchor. The findings inventory records that it is not a comparison confirmed by the principal investigator; a model panel is triage and not validation, and no claim of reception or contact follows.
lessons: Localised clusters on one Hume section are the strongest signal for escalation.
statistics: Pairs in the localised cluster: 8 | Retained by the panel as strong advisory cases: 6 of 8 | Retention under the stricter rule: cluster against dispersed sample: about 75% against 11%

title: Wide-net audit and report on a cleaned Recherche
question: Does a wider candidate net on a cleaned text recover the Malebranche loci the fixed top fifty missed?
what_was_done: A cleaned, section-repaired text of the Recherche was compared with Hume using a much wider candidate net than the fixed top fifty. Eighty-six pairs were audited at paragraph level under the locked rubric, and a scholar-facing report followed with a curated context packet.
result_summary: 32 of 86 audited pairs passed, 11 were borderline and 43 were filtered. Pairs found only by the wider net passed at 22 of 35, against 10 of 50 for the fixed top fifty, and three contact clusters were recorded (EHU 7, THN 1.3.14, THN 1.4.2) as audit findings and 'not historical-influence claims'. The cleaned text used here was later quarantined for editorial apparatus; the records read do not say how that bears on these figures.
lessons: The wider net surfaced audit-confirmed contact at about three times the rate of the fixed top fifty in this audit. | Calibration findings from one report are kept as calibration data and not promoted to general rules.
statistics: Pairs audited: 86 | Passed / borderline / filtered: 32 / 11 / 43 | Pass rate, pairs found only by the wider net: 22 of 35 | Pass rate, fixed top fifty: 10 of 50 | Priority test pairs passing: 12 of 18

title: Two-family model review of four Entretiens cases
question: Do two frontier model families agree, reading the sources, on four cases a routing model had promoted?
what_was_done: Four Hume and Entretiens pairs promoted in a routing pilot were assembled into a passage-bearing dossier. One frontier model reviewed them and a second, from another family, reviewed them blind; the two reviews were kept separate.
result_summary: Two cases were concordant as strong (one with a qualification about the source), one was concordant as strong with a qualification about a bridging step, and one was disputed in strength and kept as secondary. The record says the counts are descriptive for this selected pilot only: not a validation rate, not catalogue-wide performance, not human expert validation.
lessons: Reviews by frontier models are triage and are preserved separately; no independent human review was available.
statistics: Cases reviewed: 4 | Concordant strong (including two with qualifications): 3 | Disputed in strength: 1

title: First four scholarly reports and a comparative research report
question: Can audited results be turned into graded, testable hypotheses for a scholar?
what_was_done: Four scholar-facing reports were written from audited results (Descartes, Arnauld, Malebranche's Recherche, Huet), each stating hypotheses, competing explanations and tests. A fifth, comparative report treated Arnauld and Malebranche together. Fifty-three named tests were then extracted from the five reports as a design for a research pipeline.
result_summary: The reports graded their hypotheses in the project's vocabulary: 'Plausible' for Descartes, Arnauld and Huet (the last localised to EHU 12) and 'Inconclusive (pipeline-limited null)' for the Recherche. The grades for Arnauld and Huet stand as recorded in April 2026 and were not re-adjudicated under the later review contract; the Recherche was audited again on a wider net in May 2026 (see that row). All four are assessments of hypotheses for testing, not conclusions about Hume's sources.
lessons: The unit of analysis shifted from individual texts to hypotheses: the system produces research programmes, not verdicts. | Each report is both a claim to be tested and a test of the instrument.
statistics: Scholarly reports: 4 | Research reports: 1 | Named tests extracted from the five reports: 53

title: Audit of Régis on causation against the Cartesian tradition
question: Are the causal doctrines in Régis that the project compared with Hume distinctive of Régis, or common to the Cartesian tradition?
what_was_done: Ten doctrine rows and a set of dependency relations were drawn from the 1691 Cours entier and compared with Descartes, Malebranche, Rohault, La Forge, Cordemoy and Arnauld, some read in primary text and some reached only through reference works. The preregistration was frozen before the comparator research, an independent reviewer's objections were applied, and documentary evidence of any historical relation was recorded separately.
result_summary: The finding is that distinctiveness of the configuration is 'unresolved': seven doctrine rows were common within the audit, two were unresolved, one was equivocal, and no distinctive variant was established. On the historical side, Hume's works never name Régis and no mention was found in the searched letters; two indirect circulation facts are recorded, and the audit states that neither establishes reading. Its ceiling is 'bounded distribution and configuration findings only'.
lessons: The rule for applying the audit's labels was written after review and is disclosed as post hoc. | 'Cartesian' is not one position: Régis was placed separately against occasionalism, partial occasionalism, concurrence and a physics-only stance. | The main coverage limit is a comparator named by the scholarship (Desgabets) that was outside the set.
statistics: Doctrine rows: 10 | Rows common within the audit / unresolved / equivocal / distinctive variant: 7 / 2 / 1 / 0 | Régis paragraphs registered before research: 34 | Reviewer objections, all applied: 1 blocking, 10 major, 5 minor

title: Two pilots of a tiered comparison-dossier workflow
kind: Pilots adjudicated by the principal investigator
question: Does a workflow of blind first reading, adversarial review and tiering put pairs worth a scholar's time at the top of a review queue?
what_was_done: A dossier workflow was designed with a claim ladder on which no influence claim can be generated mechanically. A first pilot built 36 candidate entries from 8 Hume targets and had them read blind. A second pilot of 45 cases added two adversarial passes by a second model in separate contexts, a repaired tiering rule, a blind pre-screen by an external model of a pre-frozen top eight with four low-tier sentinels, and then a review of eight cases by the principal investigator.
result_summary: The preregistered criterion of the second pilot was met: the external pre-screen judged 7 of the pre-frozen top 8 worth human review now (6 required) and none of the 4 sentinels. The principal investigator then advanced 7 of 8 cases and declined 1, a disagreement the record says is 'preserved, not reconciled'. The permitted claim is a 'development and workflow-utility result' about queue ordering, not validation of retrieval; no French case reached the principal investigator's slate.
lessons: A first reader's negative must not be able to veto an adversarial positive; the tiering rule was repaired for this. | Two passes by one model family in separate contexts are never independent evidence. | Citable locators are a precondition: the first pilot was blocked until every candidate had a citation-grade source locator.
statistics: First pilot: entries characterised as substantive textual relations: 24 of 36 (16 English, 8 French) | Second pilot: first adversarial pass weakened, supported, rejected: 40, 5, 0 of 45 | Second pilot: repaired tiers one to four: 3, 20, 9, 13 | Pre-frozen top eight judged worth human review now: 7 of 8 | Low-tier sentinels judged worth review: 0 of 4 | principal investigator review: advance now and do not advance: 7 and 1 of 8

title: First La Flèche pilot with principal investigator adjudication
kind: Pilots adjudicated by the principal investigator
question: Do four well-prepared La Flèche works yield comparisons with Hume that survive the principal investigator's reading, and where in the candidate lists do they sit?
what_was_done: Four works (Malebranche's Entretiens, Fénelon's Démonstration, Crousaz's Logique, Régis's Cours entier tome 1) were run through the French retrieval default with a full record of pre-cap candidates and convergence. Thirty-three units were selected under a rule frozen before any retrieval output existed and read once by a model analyst. The principal investigator then read the four cases the model had rated strong.
result_summary: Twelve of 33 units were model-positive and 4 model-strong; the principal investigator confirmed all four as strong. The permitted conclusion is that the pilot produced one principal investigator-confirmed strong comparison that is new at the level of the relation (in Régis), one principal investigator-confirmed specific refinement within earlier Hume and Malebranche terrain on the theory of ideas, and principal investigator confirmation of two already positive Malebranche terrains. Not claimed: influence, novelty to scholarship, or a validated precision rate. Three contact zones were recorded, all in the Entretiens.
lessons: These were selected model-strong cases, not a representative sample: no precision estimate follows from them. | Three of the four strong cases were surfaced only through the convergence record, not the capped queue. | The highest yield came on the terrain the project had already read most (Malebranche's Entretiens); all six positives with no earlier adjudication in the project came from the other three works.
statistics: Units read: 33 | Model-positive units: 12 (4 strong, 8 worth follow-up) | Model-strong cases confirmed strong by the principal investigator: 4 of 4 | Confirmed strong cases new at the level of the relation: 1 of 4 | Strong cases with no carrying pair in the capped top fifty: 3 of 4 | Contact zones recorded by the principal investigator: 3

title: Second La Flèche pilot: deeper convergence reading
kind: Pilots adjudicated by the principal investigator
question: Do convergence points deeper in the candidate lists of three works still yield comparisons that survive the principal investigator's reading?
what_was_done: With no new retrieval, 22 fresh units were sampled from the first pilot's records for Régis, Fénelon and Crousaz: capped-queue controls, early convergence points on each side, and points at about 10% and 25% of the way down the convergence order. Routing repairs kept Latin-to-Latin pairs and apparatus out of primary slots. A model analyst read the units and the principal investigator read the three rated strong.
result_summary: Seven of 22 units were model-positive and 3 model-strong; the principal investigator confirmed all three as strong, one of them (Crousaz on vivacity and assent) only after a first verdict of 'needs more context' and a supplemental packet of Hume's text. The permitted conclusion is that Régis 'now warrants treatment as a substantive La Flèche comparison object for further targeted reading'. The ledger adds that this is not to be reported as a three-in-three precision estimate.
lessons: Returns diminished between about the 10% and 25% positions in this sample; three units per band is not a threshold estimate. | principal investigator review changed an outcome: one case was first deferred and confirmed only after a governed supplement. | Routing repairs kept Latin magnets out of primary slots, but marginal-gloss splices cannot be detected automatically.
statistics: Units read: 22 | Model-positive units: 7 (3 strong, 4 worth follow-up) | Model-strong cases confirmed strong by the principal investigator: 3 of 3 (one after supplementation) | Positives with no carrying pair in the capped top fifty: 6 of 7 (all 3 strong) | Positives at the 10% position and the 25% position: 2 of 3 and 0 of 3 | Positives among capped-queue controls: 0 of 3

title: First wave of a search in new works: not executable
kind: Pilots adjudicated by the principal investigator
question: Can the pilot method be run on a roster of works the project's models had not yet been exposed to?
what_was_done: A roster of new works was proposed for a search for passage pairs worth a scholar's reading, and was checked against the project's eligibility rule. No retrieval and no reading took place.
result_summary: The wave was recorded as not executable: after the eligibility check fewer than five eligible works remained. It was closed without any run. The findings document files this with the conclusion that a powered test of prospective discovery is not feasible in this library as things stand.
lessons: Eligibility must be checked before the scholarly roster is preregistered.
statistics: Eligible works remaining after the check: fewer than 5

title: Second wave: five further works, sampled at depth
kind: Pilots adjudicated by the principal investigator
question: Can the instrument route a scholar to comparisons worth close reading among pairs the project had not yet labelled, in five further works, and at what depth do they lie?
what_was_done: A stratified sample of 99 previously unlabelled pairs was drawn from five works (Buffier, Hartsoeker, Bonichon, Péan de La Croullardière, Marandé) across the capped surface, cap-suppressed pairs, deeper pairs and convergence anchors. A model reader labelled them blind and the principal investigator approved the labels without change; 27 units were escalated. Final adjudications were drafted by a model adviser and approved by the principal investigator without change.
result_summary: Of 27 escalated units the final adjudication retained 7 as strong and 8 as moderate, left 1 needing more context and set 11 aside. The permitted claim is that the instrument 'can route scholars to previously project-unlabelled comparisons worth close reading', not novelty to scholarship, recall, coverage, contact or influence. Five of the nine first-pass strong labels came from deep in the candidate lists and none from the capped surface.
lessons: Depth, not breadth, carried the yield; the record says explicitly that this is not a threshold or stopping rule. | Final adjudications were principal investigator judgments by adoption of a model draft; project novelty does not map to novelty in scholarship. | Sampling the capped surface after excluding labelled rows samples its unlabelled frontier, not its top.

title: Direct-reading calibration on three French authors
question: When retrieved pairs are read directly in context, which survive as distinctive and which are only resonance within a shared field?
what_was_done: Under a written protocol for direct reading, retrieved pairs for Burlamaqui and Boullier were read in context and adjudicated, and a pair between Hume's first Enquiry section 7 and Éclaircissement XV of Malebranche's Recherche was reviewed by the principal investigator. Outcomes were entered in a registry of reviewer-routed pairs.
result_summary: The record calls the outcome 'bidirectional calibration'. Burlamaqui and Boullier were retrieval-positive but negative on direct reading and were classed as field resonance. The Malebranche pair was a distinctive positive, though the record limits its standing to that of a pair the principal investigator had already reviewed and banked. Direct reads made with knowledge of the project context are advisory only, and the cleaned Recherche text was quarantined for editorial apparatus.
lessons: Retrieval-positive and close-read-negative is a real class: shared field vocabulary without a specific relation. | Close reads may reject, object or route, but not certify.
statistics: Authors read as field-resonance negatives: 2 | Pairs banked as a distinctive positive: 1

title: Ledger of disagreements among six model readers
question: When model readers disagree about a comparison, do they disagree about what the texts say or about the criterion for retaining it?
what_was_done: Thirty-six cases from the regression study were re-read under fresh blind identifiers by a further model reader operated by the principal investigator. The recorded judgments and rationales of six readers were laid side by side, and a ledger of propositions separated textual adequacy, philosophical relationship, potential for a convergence zone and historical inquiry. A dossier of 15 cases was prepared for adjudication.
result_summary: No disagreement was found in the readers' descriptions of the texts in any of the 36 cases (which is not an independent check that the descriptions are correct); 22 disagreements reduced to a named proposition, 4 remained substantive and 4 were limited by the adequacy of the text. The record's phrase is 'interpretive agreement, criterial disagreement'. Eight 'promising' and ten 'provisional' preliminary convergence zones were listed. No adjudication outcome is recorded in the ledger entry.
lessons: A convergence zone is a repeated pattern of relationships across a region, a hypothesis to investigate and not a measure of influence; a single promising comparison is only a pair-level signal. | A discount for period commonplaces is a contextual qualification only; a bridge that rests on form alone is insufficient. | Majority voting among model readers is never used.
statistics: Cases in the ledger: 36 | Disagreements clarified to a named proposition: 22 | Disagreements remaining substantive: 4 | Disagreements limited by text adequacy: 4 | Preliminary convergence zones: promising and provisional: 8 and 10

title: Four-case diagnostic: assessment, cross-family critique and reply
question: Do nominated comparisons from the Recherche survive when read in context, attacked by a critic from another model family and defended?
what_was_done: The four completed assessments from the ended pilot were sent, with the full primary-text context, to a critic from a different model family. A fresh analyst then replied to each objection by conceding it, answering it with a located quotation, or leaving it unresolved. Every quotation in the replies was checked mechanically.
result_summary: At the level of the nominated passages no reading called any case substantive: one was agreed topical, one agreed partial, and two were disputed between partial and topical. What survived were relationships to doctrines or traditions, and those judgments rest partly on what the model recalls and were not examined by a critic. The record states that all of it is model-assisted assessment, that no human has validated any of it, and that 'nothing below is adopted as final'.
lessons: Reading in context is where the evidence is: in each case the deciding passage lay outside the nominated paragraphs. | Passage level and doctrine level are different questions; 'common source' hides three separate claims. | A critic from another model family changes the result where the same family reading twice had not.
statistics: Cases: 4 | Cases substantive at passage level in any reading: 0 | Objections and listed mistakes put: conceded, answered, unresolved: 19, 4, 8 of 31 | Strong interpretations cut by the critic: 9 of 15 | Quotations in the replies checked, none failing: 92 | Model tokens per case, assessment and reply: about 260,000

title: Contextual reading of sixteen pending comparisons
question: How do the sixteen comparisons held as model-positive and awaiting the principal investigator's reading fare when each is read once in context?
what_was_done: Each of the 16 comparisons (in Régis, Fénelon, Crousaz and Malebranche's Entretiens) was read once by a fresh model analyst from a pre-built case file with fifteen paragraphs of context and the Hume section. Judgments were given separately for the passage and for the doctrine, and every quotation was checked against the supplied text. No critic, literature search or page image was used.
result_summary: At passage level none of the 16 was rated substantive: 10 were partial and 6 topical. At doctrine level 11 were substantive and 5 partial, but those judgments rest partly on the analyst's general knowledge. 'No nomination survived as worded': in 10 cases the analyst preferred a different Hume paragraph in the same section. These are single model assessments that no critic attacked and no human validated; a doctrine-level judgment is a claim about the structural relation of positions, not about Hume's reading.
hume_scope: THN Book 1 sections, THN 2.2.6, THN 2.3.10 and EHU 4
lessons: The pending nominations mostly pointed at the right neighbourhood and the wrong sentence. | The doctrine level is where the content is, and it is the weaker evidence. | Most of what is shared is common property of the Cartesian tradition, so the comparison bears on that tradition, not on this book in particular.
statistics: Valid assessments: 16 (1 further run invalid) | Passage level: substantive, partial, topical: 0, 10, 6 | Doctrine level: substantive, partial, topical: 11, 5, 0 | Cases where the analyst preferred another Hume paragraph in the section: 10 of 16 | Stance: opposition, different target, qualification, support: 7, 6, 3, 0 | Quotations identical to the supplied text: 325 of 325

title: Blind contextual reading of thirteen principal investigator-confirmed comparisons
question: Does a single contextual reading by a model analyst, not told of the confirmation, agree with the principal investigator's confirmed comparisons?
what_was_done: Thirteen comparisons the principal investigator had confirmed (ten strong, three moderate) in Régis, Buffier and Hartsoeker were each read once in context by a fresh model analyst who was not told they had been confirmed. Two further confirmed cases were not included in this batch. Quotations were checked against the supplied text.
result_summary: At passage level 2 were rated substantive (both in Régis), 6 partial, 4 topical and 1 unsupported; at doctrine level 8 substantive and 5 partial. By work, all five Régis cases came out partial or substantive, Buffier three partial and one topical, and none of the four Hartsoeker cases above topical. The record says 'these disagreements are preserved, not resolved': one model reading does not overturn a principal investigator confirmation, and the two were made on different evidence.
lessons: The cheap single-pass form discriminates: across 29 cases it returned every passage-level outcome and rejected one confirmed case outright. | Where the analysts and the earlier confirmations part most sharply is a question for a Hume scholar, not for another model pass. | The principal investigator's confirmations were made on the nominated pair, the analysts' readings on the pair in context; the two are different evidence.
statistics: Assessments: 13 (2 further confirmed cases not included) | Passage level: substantive, partial, topical, unsupported: 2, 6, 4, 1 | Doctrine level: substantive, partial: 8, 5 | Passage level by work: Régis, Buffier, Hartsoeker: 2 substantive and 3 partial; 3 partial and 1 topical; 3 topical and 1 unsupported | Quotations identical to the supplied text: 238 of 238

title: Six-case pilot of contextual assessment: ended early
question: Can model analysts assess a nominated comparison by reading it in full context and checking literature and edition history?
what_was_done: Six cases drawn from the Recherche discovery work, two of them concealed calibration cases, were each given to a fresh model analyst with the surrounding text. Analysts could search for secondary literature. Quotations in each finished assessment were checked mechanically against the supplied text.
result_summary: The pilot 'was not completed': it ended under its stop rule after three web fetches were denied. Four assessments were finished and preserved as exploratory (one with a documented procedural exception), one was written after its agent had been stopped and is held unused, and one was never written. All quotations in the four finished assessments matched, which the record says is 'not verification of any philosophical conclusion'.
lessons: A denied tool call stops that agent, and nothing is sent to a stopped agent. | Edition history is not a task for an analyst agent. | Matching quotations must never be reported as verification of an interpretation.
statistics: Cases planned: 6 | Assessments completed: 4 | Quotations checked in the four, all identical: 105 | Tokens used by the six agent runs: about 921,000

title: Two putative convergence zones in Régis, read in context
question: Around two confirmed Régis comparisons, is there a larger zone of repeated convergence with Hume and not only a single pair?
what_was_done: A mechanical profile first marked stretches of a book whose paragraphs lie nearest one Hume section; it used no model and stands outside the fixed pipeline. A fresh model analyst, not shown that profile or the earlier assessments, then read a wide stretch of Régis against the Hume section for each of two cases, listing every link with its relation, rating and specificity. A working rule for what counts as a zone was fixed before any reading.
result_summary: Both stretches met the working rule: Régis on testimony against the first Enquiry section 10 broadly (13 links, mostly opposition), and Régis on divisibility against Treatise 1.2 narrowly ('real but thin'). In the testimony zone the analyst rated every strong link as common to a seventeenth-century apologetic genre, so the record says the convergence is with the genre and 'not shown to be with Régis'. Both are putative zones from one model reading each, with no critic, literature check or page-image verification.
lessons: The unit worth reporting is the zone, with its pairs inside it: isolated pairs understate one zone and overstate the other. | Finding the exact pair is hard; finding the stretch may not be. The record marks this as a claim to test, not an established one. | Whether a treatment is distinctive or a transcription of a common source is a question for the literature and the rest of the library.
statistics: Testimony zone: links rated partial or better: 13 (7 substantive) | Testimony zone: Régis paragraphs and Hume paragraphs in those links: 13 and 14 | Divisibility zone: links rated partial or better: 4 (2 substantive) | Quotations identical to the supplied text: 45 of 45 and 37 of 37 | Candidate stretches found mechanically in seven works: 215, of which 192 sit on a single Hume paragraph | Candidate stretches remaining once those are excluded: 23

title: Blind retrieval test on Bayle's Dictionnaire
question: Does fixed retrieval surface contacts between Bayle's Dictionnaire and Hume that were listed as expected before the results were seen?
what_was_done: The four tomes of the Dictionnaire were prepared and run under frozen retrieval. Expected contacts were registered in advance and the analysis was blind to them until the retrieval was fixed. Pairs were then aggregated to parent paragraphs and a small number audited.
result_summary: Of 17 contacts registered in advance as strongly expected, 10 appeared in the top fifty and 12 in the top five hundred. Eight parent-pair observations were recorded; one (an article on Spinoza against THN 1.4.5) was admitted 'as strong structural homology' after exposure and one was blocked for contamination. The record allows 'no precision / FPR / global-instrument-quality claim' and no influence claim; the subproject has been dormant since 31 May 2026.
lessons: A blinding checklist written for this test was kept as a durable procedure.
statistics: Strongly expected contacts found in the top fifty: 10 of 17 | Strongly expected contacts found in the top five hundred: 12 of 17 | Parent-pair observations recorded: 8 (1 blocked for contamination)

title: Systematic deep reading of Régis's Cours entier
question: Is the comparison terrain between Régis and Hume recurrent across the book, and is any of it specific to Régis?
what_was_done: With no new retrieval, 30 fresh units were drawn from the first pilot's records on a grid of four quarters of the book, three depths of the convergence order and two directions, plus six capped-queue controls. A model analyst read them, mapped recurring terrains and wrote a model-side audit of distinctiveness. The principal investigator then read the three cases rated strong.
result_summary: Seven of 30 units were model-positive and 3 model-strong; the principal investigator confirmed all three as strong. The model-side assessment was 'mixed': coherent, recurring terrain on causation and on space and quantity, but distinctiveness 'mostly tradition-mediated or unresolved'. The ledger's wording is that confirmation 'strengthens the evidence that Régis has recurrent, philosophically substantive comparison terrain with Hume. It does not establish Régis-specific configurational distinctiveness.'
hume_scope: THN 1.3.7; THN 1.2.2 and 1.2.4; THN 1.3.14 and EHU 7 (confirmed cases)
lessons: Absence of a comparison record for other authors is not evidence that a position is specific to this one. | The pattern by depth is descriptive falloff, not a threshold. | Further deep reading of one author adds tradition-mediated recurrence until the distinctiveness question is settled from outside.
statistics: Units read: 30 | Model-positive units: 7 (3 strong, 4 worth follow-up) | Model-strong cases confirmed strong by the principal investigator: 3 of 3 | Units judged merely topical: 23 of 30 | Positives by depth: early, about 10%, about 25%, capped controls: 3 of 8, 2 of 8, 1 of 8, 1 of 6 | Positives strictly outside the capped top fifty: 5 of 7 (all 3 strong)

title: Discovery reading of the Recherche, first tranche
question: Can a cheap reading sweep of chapters of the Recherche, followed by a card-based pass and a blind check, nominate passages worth pairing with Hume?
what_was_done: Five divisions of volume one (181 paragraphs) were swept by a model reader that saw only Hume's section headings, three reads per window. A second pass with a card inventory of Hume's paragraphs proposed specific partners, and a second model of the same family rated each against random decoys. A project adviser model then rated the resulting dossier entries.
result_summary: The sweep kept 50 zones touching 45 of the 181 paragraphs. After correction, the blind check passed all 50: 'as a filter the check removed nothing'. The adviser rated 18 of 23 new entries worth examining, but it had read the dossier under a wrong label and its ratings are 'not independent validation or final scholarly adjudication'. The summary states that nothing in it is a finding about influence or novelty.
hume_scope: Treatise, first Enquiry and some Essays; only part of Hume's text was available to the readers
lessons: The blind check separates nominations from random paragraphs and does little more: it is a floor, not a ranking. | Readers and checker from one model family give stability, not corroboration. | A reviewer who compares a summary with files written by the same tool will not catch that tool's error.
statistics: Paragraphs swept: 181 | Model calls, all completed: 212 | Nominations, zones, zones kept: 260, 90, 50 | Zones passing the blind check (corrected): 50 of 50 | Random decoys scored 0 and 1 (none higher): 86 and 14 of 100 | Zones where the card pass changed the partner (corrected): 23 of 50 | Adviser ratings of new entries: worth examining, topical, wrong: 18, 5, 0

title: Discovery reading of the Recherche, second tranche and blind review
question: Does the discovery sweep hold up on ten whole chapters, and does a blind reader from another model family agree with its nominations?
what_was_done: Ten whole chapters of volume one (316 paragraphs) were swept, passed through the card-based reader and checked against random and same-section decoys. A reader from a different model family then rated 126 Hume paragraphs against 57 passages with scores, tiers and routes hidden and with unmarked controls mixed in. The results were reconciled with the hidden routes.
result_summary: All 66 entries passed the same-family check, and the blind reader rated 86 of 108 proposed paragraphs worth examining against 4 of 18 unmarked controls. The addendum then records that when four cases were read in context none was substantive at the level of the nominated passages: 'the high rates in the blind review did not predict this', and the tiers 'should not be read as rankings of scholarly worth'. Discovery sweeps of the Recherche were stopped; no third tranche is planned.
hume_scope: Treatise, first Enquiry and some Essays; only part of Hume's text was available to the readers
lessons: The blind check scores; it does not filter: it removed nothing in either tranche. | A paragraph from the same section that nobody proposed is not a clean negative. | The comparison of routes is not cards against no cards: every paragraph shown was picked with the cards.
