title: Test of a cross-encoder reranker for cross-register matches
question: Can a reranking model bring a doctrinal match that differs in vocabulary into the scored set?
what_was_done: Four experiments added a cross-encoder reranker to the retrieval step under several merge designs: direct replacement, backfill at three budgets, and a relaxed cap on pairs per Hume paragraph. The test target was the Malebranche occasionalism passage the fixed pipeline had missed.
result_summary: The reranker surfaced real cross-register material, moving the missed passage far up the list, and 8 of 15 pairs it added passed scoring. Under every merge design tested, the target pair still failed to survive the budget and diversity caps into the scored dossier. The method was 'not cleared for production integration' and was parked.
lessons: The reranker showed real signal, but under every design tested the target pair did not survive the budget limits and diversity caps into the scored dossier.
statistics: Experiments: 4 | Reranker-added pairs that passed scoring: 8 of 15 | Share of passing pairs in merged dossiers, before and after: 34.0% to 38.3%

title: Development of the fixed retrieval configuration
question: Which retrieval unit and combination of channels best recovers documented parallels across French and English?
what_was_done: Window sizes, sentence-bounded spans, three retrieval channels and their fusion were varied one at a time on two development texts with documented parallels to Hume, in blinded comparisons. The best configuration was frozen as the reference baseline for all later texts.
result_summary: The record's wording is that the hybrid configuration 'is the best tested cross-lingual configuration' (provisional) and that 'no single configuration recovers all three documented Perinetti parallels'. It also records that eight single-variable retrieval experiments found no improvement. Provisional findings add that the two lexical channels are 'largely non-functional cross-lingually'.
lessons: Retrieve narrow, interpret wide: the retrieval unit and the scoring unit should differ. | Hub passages dominate more in cross-lingual than in same-language retrieval.
statistics: Single-variable experiments finding no improvement: 8 | Documented parallels recovered by any single configuration: fewer than 3 of 3

title: Bridge test of the register gap between Arnauld and Malebranche
question: Why does Arnauld's polemic match Hume where Malebranche's own statement of the same doctrines does not?
what_was_done: Triplets of passages were assembled in which Arnauld, Malebranche and Hume address the same doctrine, and the embedding similarity of each French author to Hume was compared. The Malebranche text was also re-run after removing editorial apparatus.
result_summary: Across four doctrine-matched triplets Arnauld was consistently closer to Hume than Malebranche was, and removing 18% apparatus from the Malebranche text made its profile worse, not better (24% to 20% as recorded). The record's conclusion is that the register gap is 'a text-level property, not an embedding model deficiency' and not a contamination problem: some documented relations are not visible at this retrieval layer.
lessons: The register gap is a representational limit, not an OCR or contamination problem. | A relation class the instrument cannot represent stays in the scholarly taxonomy as a known blind spot; it is not excluded from the benchmark.
statistics: Doctrine-matched triplets: 4 | Apparatus removed in the clean rerun: 18% | Profile figure before and after cleaning, as recorded: 24% to 20%

title: Capacity test of the fixed top-fifty list
question: Does a fixed list of fifty pairs hide substantive material when a text's points of contact with Hume are many and dispersed?
what_was_done: For an English comparison text with many documented points of contact with Hume (Locke's Essay), the candidate list was extended from fifty to one hundred pairs and re-inspected, and a dense-only variant was tried. The test was run on the English track but governs the French method.
result_summary: A well-known locus (personal identity, THN 1.4.6) was absent from the first fifty pairs despite the highest similarity in the corpus and appeared only when the list was extended to one hundred; the extension contained substantive material, not noise. The record's conclusion is that a list of fixed length is fundamentally mismatched to texts whose points of contact are many and dispersed. A wider-net layer was added in response; it extends the fixed list and does not replace it.
lessons: Three kinds of diffuse profile (weak, pervasive and blocked) look alike on a profile map and need pair-level inspection. | Ranks 51 to 100 contained substantive material, not noise.
statistics: Substantive Locke pairs confirmed in audit: 7 or more, across 7 Hume sections

title: Tests of a second embedding model for French retrieval
question: Would a different embedding model retrieve French material better than the production model?
what_was_done: After an English trial in which a second embedding model surfaced more high-specificity candidates than the production model, the second model was tested as a replacement for the dense channel on French texts against the calibration registry. A later provenance audit re-examined that comparison, and a blind confirmation run considered a narrower auxiliary role.
result_summary: As a replacement the second model 'failed': it recovered 8 of 27 positive anchors, although it preserved both validated clusters and reduced negatives by 61.8%. The comparison was later found circular, because the registry had been shaped by the production model. The model was ratified only as a triggered auxiliary lens for high-risk French settings, always to be compared against the full production stack and 'never evidence by itself'.
lessons: No tested dense model beats the full production stack on known terrain. | A result on English texts does not establish readiness for French.
statistics: Positive anchors recovered by the second model as replacement: 8 of 27 | Validated clusters preserved: 2 of 2 | Reduction in negatives: 61.8% | English trial, high-specificity cases per 24: production, second and third models: 6, 11 and 8

title: English and French Huet as a cross-language test line
question: Can the English and French versions of one work be aligned to test retrieval across languages on deeper candidate pools?
what_was_done: Deeper candidate pools were generated for six items including the Huet text in both languages, after a reproduction check on Huet passed. An attempt was then made to map aligned passages between the English and French versions.
result_summary: The mapping attempt was stopped and not integrated: an independent review found that it violated a passage-free rule, and even remediated it would have yielded only about two high-confidence anchors. The principal investigator suspended the line on 20 June 2026 and resumed the discovery and close-reading loop.
statistics: Items in the deeper-pool run: 6 | High-confidence anchors the mapping could have yielded: about 2

title: Search for strong pairs suppressed by the output caps
question: Did the caps on the scored list hide strong pairs inside French texts that had already been processed?
what_was_done: Pairs suppressed by the caps were inventoried and a 34-item sample drawn, with known magnet pairs included as controls. The cap screen was re-derived on a text restricted to the author's own voice, and 14 suppressed pairs were then scored by the fixed scorer under a bounded authorisation.
result_summary: Recorded as 'negative + cautionary': no scored pair reached the range of the one known suppressed positive, and the magnet controls scored as high as the candidates, so a bare passing score is 'the noise floor' at that depth. The known case itself was confirmed as real on the clean text and not a contamination artefact. The record limits the negative to the processed Recherche and Éclaircissements material; other works and unprocessed books were not tested.
lessons: At cap-suppressed depth a passing score is the noise floor: magnets and commonplaces pass too. | Filtering after the fact is not faithful to the method; the cap screen has to be re-run on the cleaned text.
statistics: Items in the sample: 34 | Cap-suppressed pairs scored: 14 | Scored pairs reaching the range of the known positive: 0 | Magnet controls passing: 3 of 4

title: Bake-off of second-generation pipeline options and reviewer check
question: Which second-generation pipeline option should run the next wave, and does looking deeper or adding a keyword channel recover known positives?
what_was_done: Pipeline options were compared on nine witnesses, deeper candidate pools and a keyword channel were checked against labelled positives, and the model reviewer used for triage was itself assessed. Six candidate cards were prepared for public display.
result_summary: One option was 'provisionally selected' as the operating default for the next wave, not as a replacement baseline. The recall check was 'executed, inconclusive, label-limited': a deeper pool of 500 and a keyword channel recovered no labelled positive beyond the fixed top fifty. In the nine-witness set about 6,400 apparatus-magnet pairs stood against 13 clean survivors. The reviewer was qualified 'only with second review', with no human gold standard.
lessons: The second-generation effort established that evidence could be recovered and displayed, not scale or any finding. | Lexical channels create magnet risk across languages from Latin, OCR debris and cognates.
statistics: Labelled positives recovered beyond the top fifty by a pool of 500 or a keyword channel: 0 | Apparatus-magnet pairs against clean survivors in the nine-witness set: about 6,400 against 13 | Public candidate cards: 6

title: Routing audit of existing top-fifty lists
question: Which pairs in existing top-fifty lists are worth routing to closer reading, and which are artefacts?
what_was_done: The committed top-fifty lists for a scoped set of four items were first regenerated to check reproducibility. A direct-read pilot of 20 pairs and a second wave of 60 then covered the queue recommended for reading, and recurring artefacts were folded back into the router as flags.
result_summary: The fixed pipeline reproduced the committed lists exactly for the scoped set. The reads accounted for the whole 79-pair recommended queue; a recurring Hume-side magnet paragraph in THN 1.3.6 was characterised as a routing artefact, and four 'plausible-remainder' candidates were parked as single-reader advisory, 'not certified'. No adoption, recall or discovery claim was made.
lessons: A surfaced pair is a routed candidate, not a truth claim; a panel of frontier models is triage, not validation.
statistics: Pairs read in the pilot and second wave: 20 and 60 | Recommended queue accounted for: 79 of 79 | Candidates parked as plausible remainder: 4

title: Sensitivity of the top fifty to how a text is windowed
question: How much does the top-fifty list for one text depend on ingestion policy and windowing, with the text held fixed?
what_was_done: One Régis text was prepared three ways: the original substrate regenerated under the pinned configuration, a version with a newer policy and windowing but the same segmentation, and a full re-ingestion. The three top-fifty lists and full candidate pools were compared without any scoring.
result_summary: Five scoring-free findings are recorded. The old pools were byte-identical to the regenerated ones; 7 of 50 old top-fifty candidates lay in regions the newer policy excludes as non-body; overlap of the top fifty between the first two versions was only 0.38 with the text held fixed; full re-segmentation changed almost nothing further (overlap 0.98); and 609 short in-body units excluded at window construction remain an open recall question. The planned scoring stage was put on hold.
lessons: Membership of the top fifty is sensitive to policy and windowing; the cut is an ordering convenience, not an evidential boundary.
statistics: Overlap of the top fifty between two windowings of the same text: 0.38 | Overlap of the top fifty after full re-segmentation: 0.98 | Old top-fifty candidates in regions later excluded as non-body: 7 of 50 | In-body short units excluded at window construction: 609

title: Lexical-channel repair on a pinned candidate pool
question: Does cleaning digits and stray tokens out of the lexical channel reduce magnet pairs in the top fifty for one work?
what_was_done: A fixed candidate pool for Malebranche's Entretiens was re-fused under a baseline and two repaired variants of the lexical channel, and descriptive metrics were computed from ids and ranks only. A blinded packet comparing the baseline with one variant was packaged for reading.
result_summary: The share of the top fifty occupied by magnet pairs was 0.58 for the baseline and 0.50 and 0.48 for the two repaired variants, with 8 known positives evaluable. The blinded packet has not been read and no adoption decision is recorded; the fixed baseline remains the reference. The record also notes that the blinding holds only for a reader without access to the repository.
lessons: Blinding that can be undone from committed files bounds the strength of any blinding claim.
statistics: Share of the top fifty occupied by magnet pairs: baseline and two variants: 0.58, 0.50, 0.48 | Known positives evaluable: 8

title: Trace run locating where fifteen known pairs were lost
question: At which stage of the engine are known development pairs lost before the top-fifty output?
what_was_done: Fifteen already-exposed development pairs between Hume and four French works were traced through the retrieval engine with instrumentation that records each stage. Post-hoc replays then asked how large the pool would have to be, under other selection policies, to keep them.
result_summary: All 15 pairs survived the first two stages and all 15 were lost at the engine's pruning stage before the top-fifty output, a loss attributed mechanically to global queueing across queries plus the cap on candidate paragraphs. The record states this is 'not a recall figure'. It was later requalified as a diagnostic of machinery, not of 15 adjudicated relations: one pair was excluded by close reading and 10 of the other 14 were labelled as not real cases under model adjudication delegated by the principal investigator.
lessons: A machinery diagnostic on candidate pairs is not evidence that the pairs are substantive relations, and is not recall. | Under pair-preserving semantics all 15 pairs are present in the relation pool and only deferred from the review queue; the historical record keeps its original label.
statistics: Development pairs traced: 15 | Pairs lost at the pruning stage: 15 of 15 | Pairs later labelled not a real case: 10 of 14 (1 further pair excluded by close reading) | Pool size at which 5, 10 and 15 pairs are first retained in replay: about 9,500, 37,000 and 111,000 paragraph pairs

title: Development case bank and stage-by-stage loss trace
question: Can a bank of development cases show at which pipeline stage known relations are lost?
what_was_done: A bank of development cases and a nine-point loss trace were designed. Execution was authorised, attempted and stopped before its first substantive run, because the planned composition could not be filled without a model call; the design was amended. A task-alignment gate for three model roles was run on 30 cases, and existing and proposed cases were labelled by model adjudication delegated by the principal investigator.
result_summary: The loss trace on the development bank has not been run (only the separate trace run on 15 pairs was), so the study 'supports no claim of any kind yet'. At the alignment gate the constructor model was aligned and both reader models were not. An unguarded copy of the gate runner then re-executed the whole gate when imported: 30 unauthorised live calls were made and the sealed response file was overwritten, with 8 of 30 response texts permanently lost; recorded verdicts and counts were unaffected. Case construction was later parked on an external scheduling dependency.
lessons: Importing a runner can execute it; execution paths need guards. | The load-bearing rule is that case construction is frozen before any retrieval outcome is seen, not that the constructor is human. | No estimate of recall for the whole library may be derived from a development bank.
statistics: Cases at the task-alignment gate: 30 | Unauthorised live calls in the runner incident: 30 | Response texts permanently lost: 8 of 30 | Existing cases labelled by delegated model adjudication: 27 accepted, 15 judged not a real case, of 42 | Remaining shortfall in class coverage: 7 cases

title: Development tests of retrieval channels for French sources
question: Which combination of retrieval channels nominates the most useful French passages for English Hume queries?
what_was_done: Judgments from the earlier utility replication were reclassified as development evidence and analysed channel by channel. Three development batches on fresh Hume targets then compared alternative channel combinations, with pooled candidates read blind by a fast model reader calibrated beforehand.
result_summary: The record's claim is that, in the development regime for English queries against French sources, a fusion of the dense channel with character n-grams and without the word-rarity channel 'is reproducibly at least as useful as' the existing combination across three batches. It adds that nothing is validated and nothing transfers to English-to-English retrieval. The forensics found the word-rarity channel below chance on this material and generic overlap not solved by any simple rank heuristic.
lessons: Findings about a retrieval channel are scoped to a language regime; a lexical channel must be tested on its own evidence in each. | A calibration set that fails becomes a tuning set; the instrument is then frozen on a disjoint one.
statistics: Fresh Hume targets in the first two development batches: 24 and 32 | Useful nominations in the top three, third batch: existing combination against two candidates: 28 against 39 and 40 | Earlier negative cases judged apparatus-like: 20 of 20 | Routing failures classed: generic overlap, attractor, commonplace: 11, 6, 5

title: Validation of the French retrieval default on unseen passages
question: Does the candidate channel combination beat the existing one on Hume targets never used in development?
what_was_done: A test set of 48 Hume passages not used in development was spent on a preregistered two-arm test. Candidates from both arms were read blind by a frozen primary model reader and by a secondary reader from the same family. An exact-commit promotion review followed.
result_summary: The preregistered test did not clear: under the primary reader the candidate was preferred on 9 targets, the comparator on 6, with 33 ties (one-sided exact p 0.304), and the recorded status is 'not validated'. A secondary reader showed a positive direction (16 to 7, p 0.047), which the record says 'does not substitute'. The combination was nonetheless promoted as the operating default, with the explicit statement that 'operational promotion does not imply validation'.
hume_scope: 48 Hume passages not used in development (not listed)
lessons: Operational promotion does not imply validation. | A test set, once spent, is never re-used, and no tuning followed the result.
statistics: Hume passages not used in development: 48 | Primary reader: candidate better, comparator better, ties: 9, 6, 33 | Primary reader: one-sided exact p: 0.304 | Secondary reader: candidate better against comparator better; p: 16 against 7; 0.047

title: Audit of where the retrieval pipeline can lose relations
question: At which stages can the retrieval pipeline silently lose a relation, and which stages cannot be observed at all?
what_was_done: A planning-phase audit traced the retrieval code, citing file and line for each finding, and passed through seven independent review passes. No experiment was run and no model was called. During the phase a self-written checking script was itself tested by an independent reviewer.
result_summary: The audit established that the dense eligibility gate of 200 is an effective ceiling on recall, that the operative read depth is 3 and not 50, that target selection queries only the first span of a Hume paragraph although 52.6% of paragraphs have more than one, and that four pipeline stages could not be observed. Its own ceiling is: 'this is a design, and it asserts nothing about retrieval performance'. The self-written checker was defeated on 20 of 25 injected faults and was deleted.
lessons: A self-authored verifier score must never substitute for independent review of doctrine, claim ceilings or experimental logic. | The benchmark describes the instrument's blind spots; it does not redefine the scholarly problem to fit the instrument.
statistics: Hume paragraphs with more than one span: 52.6% | Independent review passes: 7 | Injected faults the self-written checker failed to catch: 20 of 25

title: Blinded tests of retrieval against a matched null floor
question: Does the fixed retrieval system put more pairs worth a scholar's reading in front of a reader than a matched null floor?
what_was_done: A blinded packet of 26 reads mixed system-selected pairs with matched null pairs; the human read the design specified was not carried out, and a frontier model read the packet as an exploratory arm. A replication then compared 48 fresh system pairs with 48 matched null twins, read by a project adviser model that knew the project and was not fully blind to condition.
result_summary: In the replication the reader placed 18 system pairs against 6 matched null pairs in a bounded reading queue (discordant pairs 16 to 4, paired lift 0.25, one-sided exact p 0.0059). The record classes this as internal calibration only: the reader was not independent, its blinding was imperfect, French-side interpretation was not independently verified, and it is 'not evidence of human scholarly utility'. In the first packet the count was 4 of 12 against 1 of 12, a margin below the design's own inspection threshold.
lessons: Three things are never to be conflated: the human read a design specifies, a model diagnostic actually performed, and any future human validation, which needs a fresh packet. | The result supports further testing of candidate nomination; it validates neither rank ordering nor magnet logic.
statistics: First packet: system against matched null items queued: 4 of 12 against 1 of 12 | Replication: system against matched null pairs judged useful: 18 against 6 of 48 each | Replication: discordant pairs: 16 to 4 | Replication: paired lift and one-sided exact p: 0.25; 0.0059 | Blind repeats agreeing: 8 of 8

title: Convergence record added alongside the capped queue
question: Can relations hidden by the output caps be recorded and surfaced without changing what the retrieval engine returns?
what_was_done: A side record was implemented that keeps, for each run, where several candidate passages converge on the same Hume passage, including pairs the caps remove from the queue. The engine's behaviour was regression-tested before and after, and the implementation was accepted and integrated.
result_summary: The implementation was accepted and integrated on 6 October 2026 with retrieval, ranking, cap and top-fifty behaviour unchanged for the reviewed scope (1,379,921 of 1,379,921 regression rows identical). Its metadata 'annotates and never adjudicates'. The findings document later records that this record surfaced every strong case of the first pilot that had no earlier adjudication in the project, and most of the second pilot's; that is newness to the project's records, not to scholarship.
lessons: Convergence is the surfacing mechanism that finds what the caps hide.
statistics: Regression rows identical before and after: 1,379,921 of 1,379,921 | Non-blocking follow-ups left open: 6

title: Regression on fifteen known positives with an overflow arm
question: Would a deeper surface with an overflow arm have shown the fifteen comparisons retained in the second wave, and would model readers keep them?
what_was_done: Five previously exposed works were re-run from frozen records through a 200-pair surface and a separately ranked overflow of the first 50 cap-skipped pairs per work. Two frontier model readers from different families judged the cases that reached them. A follow-up diagnostic re-ran one reader on 36 cases through different interfaces, framings and effort settings.
result_summary: Of the 15 known positives, 9 reached a tested surface and 4 reached the frontier readers; the second reader retained 3 of those 4 and the reference reader none. The diagnostic found that the divergence between the two readers 'is not an execution-surface artefact'. Which reader is closer to scholarly judgment is recorded as indeterminate, and the claim is retrospective regression on exposed works: 'not recall, not coverage, not a prospective or discovery test, not human validation'.
lessons: The overflow size was fixed after the earlier positions were known, so the overflow arm is regression evidence only. | Two readers given the same instruction and form can diverge in one direction; neither is inferred to be correct.
statistics: Known positives reaching a tested surface: 9 of 15 | Known positives reaching the frontier readers: 4 of 15 | Of those 4, retained by the second reader and by the reference reader: 3 and 0 | Diagnostic: same dispositions across interface, framing and effort contrasts: 30, 32 and 28 of 36

title: Proof-of-mechanism test of reading with an inventory of Hume
question: Does a model reader find known Hume partners for passages of the Entretiens more often when it holds a card inventory of Hume's paragraphs?
what_was_done: An inventory of 1,361 short cards, one per available Hume paragraph, was built by a model. Readers then read windows of the Entretiens either with the inventory or with section headings only, five runs per arm, and their nominations were scored against five targets the principal investigator had ratified, one of them a control. A lookup probe and an ablation with the target cards removed were also run.
result_summary: The test was closed as 'precondition failed', with no repeat: the control case was detected in none of the runs in either arm, so by design the test 'measured its own harness or inventory and not the mechanism' and supports no conclusion for or against the method. The record adds that, had the control held, the design's table would have read stop, since the inventory arm found no more than the plain arm. The principal investigator's two rating sheets were still outstanding at closure, and the closure record says they cannot change the verdict.
hume_scope: Five target passages fixed in advance (not listed)
lessons: A preregistered size ceiling was exceeded through the implementer's estimating error; continuing required a recorded deviation authorised before any reading outcome existed. | Reviews by an adviser that knew the design and the outcome are disclosed project reviews, not independent validation. | For future designs only: a passage may have more than one defensible Hume partner.
statistics: Runs detecting the control case, inventory arm and plain arm: 0 of 5 and 0 of 5 | Runs detecting the two detected targets, inventory arm against plain arm: 3 against 5; 5 against 4 | Lookup probe answered exactly: 29 of 30 (27 required) | Model requests, all completed: 392 | Inventory size against the preregistered ceiling: about 132,000 tokens against 120,000

title: Scoring design and choice of scoring model
question: How should structural similarity be scored so that richer annotation does not distort the score, and which model can do it?
what_was_done: Two extraction prompts were separated so that the structural score uses only the core claim, argument move, concept pairs and discourse markers, while a richer extraction feeds the annotation of stance. A blinded review panel compared outputs on two corpora. A more capable model was tried as scorer, and in May 2026 a frontier model was tried under the structured audit prompt.
result_summary: The record states that 'decoupled scoring generalized across the two tested corpora' and it became the fixed scoring design. A more capable scoring model was rejected because it passed 36 of 36 pairs with no discrimination, and the later frontier-model trial passed 16 of 16. The record's own summary is that model capability is 'non-monotonic' for this triage task.
lessons: Richer extraction improves annotation but destabilises structural scoring when fed into the score. | The choice of scoring model is a pipeline parameter that must be tested per model.
statistics: Pairs passed by the rejected more capable scoring model: 36 of 36 | Pairs passed by a frontier model under the structured audit prompt: 16 of 16 | Extracted quotations verified in development: 144 of 144, no hallucination

title: Simplified promoter model as an attention signal
question: Can a cheap model's simplified judgment serve as a reliable signal of which pairs deserve attention?
what_was_done: After the failure of a small model as a gate, a simplified promoter schema was designed and a baseline run on synthetic cases with three repetitions. Later versions were validated on English comparison texts in several cycles. The real-corpus phase was prepared but not authorised.
result_summary: On the English validation one version's precision advantage reversed on unseen data (from +25 to -5 points) while recall held; another version's ordinal attention score correlated with audit scores (rank correlation 0.676 on 341 pairs). Transfer to the Bayle material, where it was to be tested next, is recorded as unverified. The layer's standing is 'signal only, no inclusion/rejection authority; not in any production pipeline'.
lessons: A precision gain seen in development can reverse on unseen material while recall holds.
statistics: Precision advantage, development against unseen data: +25 against -5 percentage points | Correlation of ordinal attention score with audit score: 0.676 (n = 341)

title: Test of a very small model as a screening gate
question: Can a very small, cheap model safely drop weak French pairs before review?
what_was_done: A very small model was asked to judge whether each of a set of benchmark pairs showed a contact zone, under a specification frozen in advance. Its decisions were graded against a calibration registry of positive and negative anchors, and its reasoning on every false drop was read.
result_summary: The model failed as a gate: it dropped 11 of 18 gold positive anchors (target zero) and retained 38.89% where at least 90% was required, although it suppressed 44 of 45 negatives. The review of its reasoning found 'coherent over-strict reasoning', not noise or hallucination. No production change followed.
lessons: Feature layers may promote or annotate, never delete. | The failure was a mismatch of standard: the model applied a strict same-target test where the benchmark calibrates a broader contact-zone standard.
statistics: Model calls: 116 | Gold positive anchors wrongly dropped: 11 of 18 (61.11%) | Negative anchors suppressed: 44 of 45 (97.78%) | Validated clusters preserved: 2 of 2

title: Dry-run of review-ordering policies that protect clusters
question: Which rule for ordering pairs for review best protects known positives while reducing the reading burden?
what_was_done: A table of machine features was assembled for 1,638 pairs across 34 candidate texts. Seven ordering policies were evaluated in a dry run against the French calibration registry, with no new model call and no change to production.
result_summary: A policy that promotes pairs belonging to a localised cluster placed 72.2% of gold positives in the top quarter of each text's queue, against 33.3% for the baseline order, and kept 12 of 15 positives that the small-model gate had wrongly dropped. It was adopted as a provisional working policy only. The registry it was graded against is itself 'calibration only, not ground truth'.
lessons: Cluster signal is the strongest current positive feature; a small-model gate used alone was net-negative.
statistics: Pair rows in the feature table: 1,638 (460 passed, 508 borderline, 670 filtered) | Policies evaluated: 7 | Gold positives in the top quarter: baseline against cluster policy: 33.3% against 72.2% | Share of queue to review for 90% gold recall: baseline against cluster policy: 98% against 84%

title: Reliability audit of machine scores on French texts
question: How often does a passing machine score on a French pair survive review by a panel of frontier models?
what_was_done: Thirty-eight pairs were sampled in strata from four French texts (Arnauld, Malebranche's Entretiens, Ramsay's Histoire de Turenne, Bergier). Three frontier models from different families each judged every pair, the judgments were aggregated mechanically, and a provisional rule for reading the scores was adopted.
result_summary: Of 18 passing pairs the panel retained 5; the record puts the false-positive rate of a passing score at 72% (13 of 18). Filtered pairs were dropped by the panel 8 times out of 8, and borderline pairs behaved like filtered ones (0 of 12 retained). The adopted rule is that the score 'remains useful as a negative filter and triage layer, not as a standalone positive selector'; it is a provisional rule on a small sample, 'not ground truth' and not qualified French philological review.
lessons: A passing score is not sufficient by itself for scholarly review; it needs a localised cluster, cross-model support or an explicit selection. | Localised clusters on one Hume section are the strongest signal for escalation. | Panel members differed in strictness, so a panel's composition is itself a methodological concern.
statistics: Pairs sampled: 38 | Passing pairs retained by the panel: 5 of 18 (28%) | Passing pairs judged false positives: 13 of 18 (72%) | Filtered pairs the panel also dropped: 8 of 8 | Borderline pairs retained: 0 of 12 | Top-scored pairs retained: 1 of 3 | Retention by text: Arnauld 25%, Entretiens 11%, Ramsay 0%, Bergier (dispersed) 11%

title: Calibration of three hosted open models as readers
question: Can any of three hosted open-weight models read French and English pairs to a preregistered operational standard?
what_was_done: Three open-weight model configurations on a shared research inference service were evaluated under one frozen setting against a preregistered, mechanically auditable floor, with two exposed regression controls. The run stopped at a preregistered stop after 63 of 208 planned calls, and later phases were not executed. Two follow-up designs were drafted.
result_summary: The qualification record states: 'None cleared that floor. Observed shortfalls were heterogeneous and dimension-specific.' Of the two regression controls, one showed unanimous divergence from a banked judgment and one unanimous preservation. It adds that 'no conclusion follows about French-language comprehension in either direction'. Of the follow-up designs, one is design-only and the other is blocked for want of an independent bilingual reference.
lessons: Failing an operational floor is not a finding about a model's comprehension of French, in either direction.
statistics: Model configurations evaluated: 3 | Configurations clearing the floor: 0 | Calls made before the preregistered stop: 63 of 208

title: Test of a structured close-reading form for model readers
question: Does a structured close-reading form let a model reader tell strong textual relations from weak ones?
what_was_done: After two attempts at principal investigator review of machine-selected pairs were stopped for burden and for a label too coarse to be useful, a nine-field form was written that requires both what two passages share and their most important difference. A blind frontier adviser read 57 pairs already judged useful by two model readers, and then a stratified sample of 60 that included pairs both had rejected. The material was English; the form was later used on French pairs.
result_summary: On the stratified sample the form produced a strictly ordered gradient across the four strata and used the whole negative range, so the recorded disposition is that the reading 'discriminates' at the negative end. On the first 57 pairs, contrast or inversion was the most frequent relation type (42 of 57). The record limits the claim to this sample: it is not a validation of retrieval and not a precision estimate.
lessons: The dominant reason these pairs repay reading is opposition, not resemblance; a single queue label had compressed that. | An all-positive result on pre-filtered material says nothing about whether a reader discriminates; a contrast set has to be read.
statistics: Pairs in the first, pre-selected reading: 57 (strong 44, moderate 13) | Pairs in the stratified test: 60 | Mean value rating in the highest, middle and lowest strata: 3.00, 2.38, 1.43 | Gap in strong-rate between highest and lowest strata, against threshold: 0.857 against 0.25 | Blind repeats agreeing on all primary fields: 12 of 12 in each reading

title: English sanity test for a routing model
question: Does any hosted open model discriminate philosophically well enough on English material to justify designing a French routing stage?
what_was_done: Three hosted open-weight models were given 108 routing calls on English philosophical pairs, with a frontier model's judgments as an advisory reference. The principal investigator then decided which configurations to retain. The test was run on English texts as a precondition for a French design.
result_summary: The permitted claim is that the experiment showed sufficient philosophical discrimination in at least one tested hosted configuration to justify designing a separately authorised exploratory routing stage for the La Flèche texts, and no more. One model was kept as primary candidate, one as an adversarial challenger, and one was retired for promoting every case indiscriminately. The record forbids saying that the models 'generally passed', that any has demonstrated French competence, or that the result is human validation.
lessons: One model was retired from routing for promoting cases indiscriminately on this test.
statistics: Routing calls completed and parsed: 108 of 108 | Cases promoted by the retired model: 36 of 36

title: Routing-model development pilot on the Entretiens
question: How does the retained routing model behave on pairs between Hume and one French dialogue?
what_was_done: Forty scored routing calls and two smoke calls were made on ten selected passages of Malebranche's Entretiens paired with Hume, for an initial route only. Forty routes from an earlier execution that had not been authorised were excluded.
result_summary: The ledger records the run as internal calibration and machine advisory routing only, with French interpretation not independently verified, and gives no outcome figures. All ten selections come from one work, so 'nothing speaks to' the catalogue or to other French authors. The 40 routes from the unauthorised execution are permanently excluded and are 'never evidence'.
lessons: An authorisation gate that checks that an authorisation exists, and not which one it is, fails.
statistics: Scored routing calls: 40 (plus 2 smoke calls) | Passages of the Entretiens selected: 10 | Routes excluded from an unauthorised execution: 40

title: Qualification series for a two-model primary review
question: Can two model reviewers, used together, escalate the comparisons the principal investigator retained in the second wave without flooding the principal investigator with negatives?
what_was_done: In three phases, model reviewers read second-wave cases blind and their escalations were compared with the principal investigator's final adjudications, which were opened only after each reviewer's output was frozen. Phase one used 12 cases; phase two used a revised rubric on 15 adjudicated cases and 20 first-pass negatives; phase three screened three alternative hosted models on the same sets under a preregistration.
result_summary: No pair of primary reviewers qualified. One hosted model escalated 12 of 12 cases in phase one, including all five that had not been pursued at adjudication, while the frontier reviewer escalated 1 of 12; under the revised rubric four of six gates failed, and the record notes that one gate passed only because an invalid output counted as an escalation. In phase three no alternative model was individually eligible. The ceiling is 'development / qualification evidence only... agreement is not truth', and further tuning on these cases was barred.
lessons: Agreement between model reviewers is not truth, and none of these measures is recall. | No further model tuning on the second wave's cases: they are development evidence and are now spent. | The failure forced a redesign: broad preparation by cheap models, a frontier-model reference, and selective authority for the principal investigator.
statistics: Phase one: cases escalated by the hosted model, a second hosted model and the frontier reviewer: 12, 2 and 1 of 12 | Phase one: cases not pursued at adjudication that the first hosted model escalated: 5 of 5 | Phase two: hosted model, adjudicated set: 11 of 14 valid outputs escalated; 1 invalid output on this set (2 across both sets) | Phase two: first-pass negatives escalated, hosted model against frontier reviewer: 9 of 20 against 0 of 20 | Phase two: gates failed: 4 of 6 | Phase three: principal investigator-strong cases escalated by the three alternatives: 2 of 4, 1 of 4, and none (4 invalid outputs) | Phase three: reviewer pairs passing: 0

title: Calibration of cheap preparation against a frontier-model reference
question: Can a cheap, broad model pass, checked against a frontier-model reference, decide which surfaced pairs go forward?
what_was_done: Six 200-pair surfaces (1,200 cases) were frozen. Hosted open models prepared the cases; the first run stopped on output-format failures for five of the six works and a separately versioned rerun requalified the lane. One frontier model served as reference reader and a second frontier model re-read 35 cases. The blind adjudication by the principal investigator that the design called for was not performed.
result_summary: Against the model reference, cases the reference retained concentrated in the prepared top ten (12 of 60, against 1 of 60 in the audit sample), with no case the reference rated strong. The second reader changed the coarse class of 13 of 35 double-read cases, so the precommitted rule stopped in its judgment zone and no operating regime was fixed. The record states that the calibration 'has no human ground truth'; a model-only assessment of 14 cases is marked provisional.
lessons: A calibration against a model reference is not a calibration against scholarly judgment. | Seven of fifteen known retained comparisons were removed by the production caps the surface applies.
statistics: Cases on the frozen surfaces: 1,200 (six works) | Reference-retained cases in the prepared top ten against the audit sample: 12 of 60 against 1 of 60 | Reference-retained cases captured in the top ten: 12 of 13 | Double-read cases whose class the second reader changed: 13 of 35 | Second-wave principal investigator-retained comparisons inside a 200-pair surface: 6 of 15 (3 in the capped top fifty)

title: Three attempts to qualify model roles before a first trace
question: Can model roles (advocate, adjudicator, translator, reviewer) be shown to do their task before any scored comparison is run?
what_was_done: Three successive exposed gates were run before a planned first substantive experiment. Each tested whether the models assigned to a role produced usable output on frozen material; the third added a machine-translation quality check on a frozen pool of 17 members.
result_summary: None of the three gates passed. In the first every request was refused; in the second the adjudicator's output was malformed and the advocate failed a context probe; in the third the translation check passed 34 items and failed 11 (7 traced to OCR, running heads or segmentation) and the reviewer qualification was negative. No scored role call was made, and the record says nothing follows about retrieval, recall or any historical relation.
lessons: Text defects (OCR, running heads, segmentation) surface as apparent translation failures.
statistics: Gates passed: 0 of 3 | Translation check: passed and failed: 34 and 11 | Translation failures traced to OCR, running heads or segmentation: 7 of 11 | Scored role calls made: 0

title: Calibration registry of French positive and negative anchors
question: Can a fixed set of known positive and negative French pairs be used to grade changes to the method in advance?
what_was_done: A registry of 106 rows was assembled from audited and panel-reviewed pairs, clusters and baselines across the French texts processed so far. Every calibration experiment of May 2026 was graded against it. A provenance audit in June examined how its rows had been found.
result_summary: The registry made predeclared evaluation possible and is recorded as 'calibration only, not ground truth'. The June provenance audit showed that its rows were shaped by the production embedding model that had found them, so that comparisons of recall between embedding models against it are circular.
lessons: A benchmark built from one retriever's own finds cannot fairly compare that retriever with another.
statistics: Rows: 106 | Positive pair anchors: 27 (20 gold, 7 strong) | Negative pair anchors: 61 (15 gold, 46 strong) | Provisional cluster candidates: 14

title: First public surface of machine-surfaced candidates
question: Can a small set of machine-surfaced candidates be shown publicly with their evidence and without any claim about Hume's sources?
what_was_done: Six candidate cards from the second-generation pipeline were published on the project's public site with page-image witnesses, then the surface was closed and frozen. Deployment remained subject to the principal investigator's approval.
result_summary: The surface was closed and frozen on 14 July 2026. Its committed wording is that the cards are 'machine-surfaced routing candidates for scholarly inspection' with no claim of influence, contact, reading, transmission, discovery, validation, recall or coverage, and that 'the cited page image is the authoritative witness for quotation'. The ledger calls the six cards 'a functioning pipeline demonstration' with no ranking claim over the catalogue.
statistics: Public candidate cards: 6

title: Public release of comparisons and convergence zones
question: Can the project's held comparisons and zones be published for historians of philosophy without source text, scores or any claim about Hume's reading?
what_was_done: New pages for zones, works, comparisons, an index by Hume section and a method page were generated from one pinned data file of locators, labels and model-written summaries. A separate model agent built the pages and another reviewed them adversarially in four passes, two returned for fixes and two cleared with notes. The site was deployed and every served page compared with the build.
result_summary: Deployed and verified as served on 17 November 2026: 203 of 203 pages byte-identical to the build. The surface carries no French source text, no quotation of Hume and no retrieval score; model readings are labelled as AI-assisted and not human-verified, and principal investigator confirmations and model readings are shown side by side. The deploy record states that no human has read the deployed wording, that three checks recommended for the testimony zone were not run, and that the automatic wording guards can be evaded.
lessons: A model reviewer's clearance is not a human reading of the pages. | Automatic wording guards can be evaded; the protection is the pinned data file, and any change to it needs the same reading.
statistics: New routes: 20 | Generated pages before and after: 183 and 203 | Comparisons, works and zones on the surface: 53, 9 and 5 (2 putative zones, 3 recorded by the principal investigator) | Served pages byte-identical to the build: 203 of 203 | First review round: blockers and major findings: 3 and 5 | Comparisons not read in context, shown by Hume section only: 24

title: Structured map of positions across nine problem spaces
question: Can philosophical positions and their dependencies be represented in a structured form that later comparisons could draw on?
what_was_done: Positions of three thinkers were proposed by model over an interpretation corpus arranged in nine problem spaces. The principal investigator adjudicated the proposals, and minimal snapshots were built over eight of the nine spaces. The work was then accepted as complete and parked.
result_summary: The principal investigator made 46 adjudications of the proposals: 34 confirmed, 10 restricted in scope and 2 needing more context; 10 proposals were quarantined. The phase is recorded as complete, accepted and 'parked, available for selective future use', with one design decision never ratified by the principal investigator. The record adds: 'This is not validation of a conversational AI system.'
statistics: principal investigator adjudications: 46 (34 confirmed, 10 scope-restricted, 2 needing more context) | Proposals quarantined: 10 | Problem spaces with a snapshot: 8 of 9

title: Cross-work candidate slate for a routing model: withdrawn
question: Which pairs from several French works should a second routing experiment be run on?
what_was_done: A slate of candidate pairs from several works was selected and packaged for a planned second routing experiment. No model call was made under the record.
result_summary: The slate was packaging only and was then barred from execution permanently after an eligibility problem was found in it. A sealed replacement set was drawn for the later blinded utility pilot. The ledger's permitted claim is 'none (not executed)'.

title: Strategic reassessment: consolidate before discovering
question: After the Recherche discovery work, where should the project's effort go next?
what_was_done: The orchestrating model wrote an assessment of the November work against the repository's findings inventory, ledger and constitution, without opening the project's internal methodological review. It listed what was and was not working and put decisions to the principal investigator.
result_summary: The assessment's conclusion is that 'the project's bottleneck is not discovery' but 'turning what has been found into evidence-grounded scholarship'. It recommended stopping discovery on the Recherche, giving the comparisons the project already holds a single contextual assessment each (beginning with the 16 awaiting the principal investigator), changing the unit of output to a doctrine-level dossier on each work and ending prospective validation experiments. The principal investigator adopted the strategy on 16 November 2026. The plan states its own limit: its cheap form had not yet been run when it was written.
lessons: The grain was wrong: the instrument is for book-level triage and a contact zone needs convergence, but the work had drifted to adjudicating single passages. | Discovery had outrun evaluation: each new method added candidates in the same unresolved state. | Whether a relationship is known, and whether a book was available, are questions for the literature and the catalogue; no reading step answers them.
